title: Condensed realization of a finite-stage Weil complex and its Frobenius operators
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $K_E\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ be an $E$-Weil complex [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], let $F$ be its global geometric Frobenius on $R\Gamma_c(Y,K_E)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], and for $n\ge1$, $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and any geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$ over $x$ (obtained from any $k_0$-embedding $\mathbf F_{q^n}\hookrightarrow k$) let $K_{E,\bar x}$ and $F_x^{(n)}$ be the stalk complex and the local operator formed at $\bar x$ by the construction of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] (which applies because $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$ for every such embedding). There is a functorial realization of this finite-stage datum as a Weil object $(K_\Omega,\phi_\Omega)$ in the bounded constructible module-object category $D^b_c(Y)[[\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)]]$ [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] for the model Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For every $n\ge1$ there are specified isomorphisms between the condensed compact-support object and the finite-matrix realization of $R\Gamma_c(Y,K_E)$, and, for every $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and every geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$, between the stalk at that same model-Frobenius-fixed geometric point $\bar x$ and the finite-matrix realization of $K_{E,\bar x}$ (the indexing by $Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ is taken relative to the chosen embedding; changing the embedding may permute the index in the fixed-inclusion bijection) [lem-zl-point-realization-coefficient-comparison, lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace], that intertwine the model-Frobenius globalOperator and stalkFrobenius [nt-assume-trace-formula] with the scalar extensions of the corresponding E-stage operators $F^n$ and $F_x^{(n)}$. The fixed points of the model Frobenius iterate are exactly the points indexed by $Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]. If the displayed E-complexes are bounded finite-dimensional, the realized condensed global and stalk objects have right duals in $D^b_c(\operatorname{Spec}k)[[\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)]]$, as objects isomorphic to finite-matrix realizations [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace]. This is a coefficient and operator comparison only: it asserts no Grothendieck--Lefschetz trace identity.

source.place: Sentence 'The trace identity ... are supplied by [thm-weil-grothendieck-lefschetz-trace]': agent-formulated coefficient/operator comparison needed to apply the batch-5 condensed trace assumption to a finite-stage E-Weil complex; not a verbatim theorem of the blueprint

proof.text: Write $M_E=\operatorname{For}K_E$, $R=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$, $A_j=R/t^j$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $g=g_Y$. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian and finite-dimensional: a field is Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] gives local Noetherianity, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] gives quasi-compactness, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] bounds the dimension. Also $\ell$ is invertible since $p\ne\ell$. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], choose the actual integral object $M$ representing $M_E$; raw rationalization has the same objects. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization] this integral category is exactly the domain of $J_Y$ in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], with the same completed coefficient sheaf and reduction functors. There is no implicit equivalence between two differently defined integral categories here. Fix a compactification $c_0$ of $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ by [sk-thm-nagata-compactification]; its base is affine, hence qcqs, and its morphism is separated finite type. Its base change $c$ to $k$ is the compactification of [def-nagata-compactification-base-change, lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change]. Use $c$ for integral and finite compact supports below, with the specified refinement comparisons to the chosen condensed functor.

source.place: Propositions 6.6.11, 6.8.11(3), 6.8.14(2); explicit checking of their scheme and coefficient hypotheses

proof.text: The reductions $M_j=M\otimes_R^LA_j$ have finite Tor amplitude. Indeed, the stratified-perfect characterization gives on each of finitely many strata a bounded finite-projective $R$-complex. Tensoring it with $A_j$ gives a bounded finite-projective $A_j$-complex in the same interval. Take the minimum and maximum over the finitely many local models; tensor with a module is then zero outside that interval. This is precisely finite Tor amplitude, while constructibility is part of membership in the integral category. Apply [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] to the arbitrary rational Weil isomorphism $\theta:Lg^*M_E\simeq M_E$: there are $N\ge0$ and $u:Lg^*M\to M$ with $\theta=t^{-N}u$. We require no Frobenius-stable lattice on which $u$ is invertible.

proof.text: Form the canonical comparisons $\kappa_j^{(r)}:L(\Phi^r)^*M_j\simeq L(g^r)^*M_j$ using [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]. They come from the relative-Frobenius isomorphisms on the pro-etale site [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site], not from a chosen scalar multiple. Construct them on simultaneous quotient diagrams: apply that same site isomorphism to each quotient and its actual quotient maps. [lem-trf-frobenius-coefficient-reduction-coherence] gives the coefficient compatibility, and [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] identifies the resulting whole-diagram pullbacks and their compositors with the specified completed pullbacks. Applying $R\lim$ defines $\kappa_R^{(r)}:L(\Phi^r)^*M\simeq L(g^r)^*M$; its inverse is the realization of the inverses on that same diagram. Multiplicativity and naturality hold before realization, by the site construction and the multiplicative law of the cited comparison. Thus these are equations of whole diagrams, rather than an inference from faithfulness of separate reductions. Put $v_r=u^{[r]}\kappa_R^{(r)}$. The rational-model theorem identifies its reductions with $\psi_{j,r}=u_j^{[r]}\kappa_j^{(r)}$ and gives $w_r=t^{-Nr}v_r[1/t]=\theta^{[r]}\kappa_E^{(r)}$. Consequently $w_r$ is the multiplicative iterate of the isomorphism $w_1$.

source.place: Tag 0F6W (relative Frobenius for weakly etale objects); rational-model proof (2), with simultaneous quotient-diagram realization supplied by the cited nodes

proof.text: For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$, define $\mathcal R_T=T^T_{E,\Omega}J_T$, where $T^T_{E,\Omega}=\Omega_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ is [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]. The equivalence $J_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] and the constructibility-preserving extension of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit] show that this is a functor to the actual bounded constructible module-object category. Use the finite-extension-valued $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$ throughout. For a $k$-morphism $h:T\to U$, let $c_h:\mathcal R_T Lh^*\simeq Lh_c^*\mathcal R_U$ be the $J$ pullback comparison followed by scalar extension. The coefficient inverse-image and composition identifications are [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. The scalar part of $c_h$ is tensor reassociation: both sides identify with $\Omega_T^c\otimes_{E_T^c}h^*J_U(-)$; on local tensors it sends $b\otimes(e\otimes m)$ to $be\otimes m$. Exact scalar extension [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-flat-coefficient-calculus] computes this on complexes. The same formula for three factors proves its unit and composition coherence. No pullback comparison for the non-$k$-linear morphism $g$ is needed in this construction.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; actual module-object and coefficient-extension identifications are the cited DAG interfaces

proof.text: Set $K_\Omega=\mathcal R_Y(M_E)$ and $\phi_\Omega=\mathcal R_Y(w_1)c_\Phi^{-1}:L\Phi_c^*K_\Omega\simeq K_\Omega$. This is an isomorphism since $w_1$ and $c_\Phi$ are. Coherence of $c_h$ and Step 3 give for every $r\ge1$ the exact iterate formula $\phi_{\Omega,r}=\mathcal R_Y(w_r)c_{\Phi^r}^{-1}$. For a morphism of $E$-Weil complexes, naturality of $\kappa_E$ gives $a w_1=w'_1L\Phi^*a$; applying the functor and $c_\Phi$ gives the corresponding equation for $\mathcal R_Y(a)$. Thus the construction is functorial. Although $u,N$ compute it, its definition is the functorial image of $\theta\kappa_E$, so replacing $u,N$ by $tu,N+1$ leaves it unchanged; the whole-diagram construction of $\kappa_E$ is natural on raw localized morphisms. This also explains why no invertible integral Weil structure was added to the hypotheses.

source.place: Clauses (1)–(4), coefficient and operator comparisons, without any trace identity

proof.text:
Let $P_E=Ra_{Y!,E}$ and $P_\Omega=Ra_{Y!,\Omega}$, with the chosen-compactification comparisons. [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization] gives the specified isomorphism $\mathcal R_s(P_EM_E)\simeq P_\Omega K_\Omega$, natural on all rational morphisms (an integral morphism divided by a power of $t$). Invert it and apply $\beta$ of [lem-zl-point-realization-coefficient-comparison] to obtain
$$b_M:P_\Omega K_\Omega\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{E,s}(C_M),\qquad C_M=\operatorname{Fib}_sP_EM_E=R\Gamma_c(Y,M_E).$$
For a $k$-point $z:s\to Y$, apply $c_z^{-1}$ and the same $\beta$ to obtain
$$b_z:Lz_c^*K_\Omega\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{E,s}(\operatorname{Fib}_sLz_E^*M_E).$$
These are specified object isomorphisms before any operator calculation. The compact-support lemma puts $P_RM$ in the integral constructible category, hence its rational point fiber is bounded finite-dimensional by the point equivalence of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The same holds for $P_RL(\Phi^r)^*M$, using Step 3 to identify that pullback with $L(g^r)^*M$. Stalk fibers are in the stated point domain by [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Thus every use of $\beta$ and every finite-matrix realization here has the required domain.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; specified compact-support and point normalization are the two cited comparison nodes

proof.text: Fix $r\ge1$. By [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], $\operatorname{Fix}(\Phi^r)$ is the finite disjoint union of $s$ indexed by $Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^r})$, using the fixed inclusion into $k$. For any other $k_0$-embedding $e:\mathbf F_{q^r}\hookrightarrow k$, the lift $z$ constructed from $x$ is still fixed: on an affine chart its values lie in $e(\mathbf F_{q^r})$, so $z(a^{q^r})=z(a)$, while $\Phi^r$ fixes $k$-scalars. Also $g^rz=zg_s^r$ because $\gamma^r$ fixes this subfield. The comparison $b_z$ is at this same lift. Changing $e$ can reindex the rational point in the fixed-inclusion bijection; it does not identify two distinct $k$-points. For example, on $Y_0=\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf F_q}$, $r=2$, and $x(t)=\alpha\in\mathbf F_{q^2}\setminus\mathbf F_q$, the inclusion gives $t\mapsto\alpha$ whereas its composition with $q$-power Frobenius gives $t\mapsto\alpha^q$. The local operator in the question is formed at the chosen lift in both cases.

source.place: Local alternating trace at rational points; correction of the fixed-point indexing for a variable embedding

proof.text:
Put $h=\Phi^r$. It is proper: [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial] gives finiteness of $\Phi$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] gives finiteness of its positive iterates, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] gives properness. Let $d_{h,K_\Omega}^{c}:P_\Omega K_\Omega\to P_\Omega Lh_c^*K_\Omega$ be the proper-unit composite. By [lem-zl-model-compact-comparison-unit], the actual compactCohomologyFrobeniusComparison in the interface named by [nt-assume-trace-formula] is exactly this map. Its globalOperator is therefore
$$G_r=P_\Omega(\phi_{\Omega,r})d_{h,K_\Omega}^{c}.$$
Only the definition of the operator is used from that interface. In particular no trace identity or duality is invoked.

source.place: Global graph-operator composite; its exact condensed implementation is the cited proper-unit normalization

proof.text:
Apply [lem-zl-proper-unit-condensed-realization] to $M$ and $h$, with $M'=Lh^*M$. Its hypotheses were verified in Steps 1, 2, 6 and 8. Write $D_{h,M,E}$ for the rational point-fiber image of its whole-tower proper-unit map. It gives
$$b_{M'}P_\Omega(c_h^{-1})d_{h,K_\Omega}^{c}=\rho_{E,s}(D_{h,M,E})b_M.$$
Naturality of $b$ for $v_r:M'\to M$, Step 5, and $E$-linearity now give
$$b_MG_r=\rho_{E,s}\bigl(t^{-Nr}C(v_r)D_{h,M,E}\bigr)b_M,$$
where $C(v_r)$ is the rational point-fiber compact-support map. By [prop-trf-graph-operator], each finite composite $P_j(\psi_{j,r})d_{h,j}$ is its graph operator. The whole-tower naturality assertion in the proper-unit realization node identifies the integral composite with the realization of those same graph maps. Clause (3) of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] identifies that realization with $U_r=R\Gamma_c(Y,u^{[r]})V_{r,M}$, where $V_r$ is geometric compact-support transport. Hence $t^{-Nr}C(v_r)D_{h,M,E}=t^{-Nr}U_r[1/t]$. This is an equality of specified maps; separate finite reductions have not been used as a conservative test on morphisms.

source.place: Clauses (1)–(4), coefficient and operator comparisons, without any trace identity

proof.text:
For clarity, compute the power before rationalizing. Write $H=R\Gamma_c(Y,-)$, $Q_r=L(g^r)^*$ and $a_r:Q_1Q_r\simeq Q_{r+1}$. By [lem-trf-integral-compact-transport-recurrence], $V_{r+1,M}=H(a_r)V_{1,Q_rM}V_{r,M}$, naturally in $M$. Since $u^{[r+1]}a_r=uQ_1(u^{[r]})$, this gives
$$U_{r+1}=H(u)H(Q_1u^{[r]})V_{1,Q_rM}V_{r,M}=H(u)V_{1,M}H(u^{[r]})V_{r,M}=U_1U_r.$$
Starting at $r=1$, induction gives $U_r=U_1^r$. The $r=1$ normalization of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] is exactly [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], including its transport arrow, so $t^{-N}U_1[1/t]=F$. Consequently $t^{-Nr}U_r[1/t]=F^r$. Substitution into Step 9 proves $b_MG_r=\rho_{E,s}(F^r)b_M$.

source.place: Clauses (1)–(4), coefficient and operator comparisons, without any trace identity

proof.text: We check the local transport normalization, since it cannot be inferred just from an object comparison. Let $z$ be a fixed lift of Step 7 and let $y\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^r})$ be the rational point to which $z$ corresponds in the fixed-inclusion bijection of [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points], so that $z=\bar y$ is the geometric point obtained from $y$ through the inclusion $\mathbf F_{q^r}\subset k$. Apply [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] with $X_0=Y_0$, $m=r$, this $y$ and $\Lambda=E$ to $K=M_E$. Its map $t_{y,r,M_E}$ consists of the $r$ successive point transports of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] on $L\bar y^*M_E$ followed by the pullback-composition identification for $g^r\bar y=\bar yg_s^r$; this is exactly the composite of $I^{[r]}_N$ and the middle isomorphism in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], with the same comparisons (that node fixes the integral ones by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], which specifies the integral composition comparisons used in the definition). Its map $\rho_{y,r,M_E}$ is the identification from $\Phi^r\bar y=\bar y$, i.e. the map $\iota$ of the stalk normalization of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], and its $\kappa^{(r)}$ is the unrescaled comparison of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], rationalized from the integral realization, which is the $\kappa_E^{(r)}$ of Step 3. It states $t_{y,r,M_E}=J_{y,E}(\kappa^{(r)}_{M_E})\rho_{y,r,M_E}$, which is $\tau_{y,r}$ of the rational-model statement. Hence $F_{y,r}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*\theta^{[r]})\circ\tau_{y,r}$ of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] is exactly the operator $F_x^{(r)}$ of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] at $z$, rather than a separately chosen conjugate. The operator formed at $z$ depends only on the $k$-point $z$ and not on the embedding through which $z$ was produced, so this covers every embedding.

source.place: Stalk normalization tau_{y,m}=(kappa^{(m)})_{y}iota and clause (4); the point-transport identification is the statement of lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization

proof.text:
In the condensed interface of [nt-assume-trace-formula], stalkFrobenius at $z$ is $Lz_c^*(\phi_{\Omega,r})$ preceded by the comparison for $\Phi^rz=z$. The pullback-composition coherence of $J$ in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] and of coefficient pullback [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], with the tensor reassociation of Step 4, transports this exact composite to the realization of the adic composite $Lz_E^*(w_r)$ preceded by the same fixed-point identity. Naturality of $\beta$ in [lem-zl-point-realization-coefficient-comparison] transports that morphism to its finite-matrix image. By Step 11 and clause (4) of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], the adic endomorphism is exactly $F_x^{(r)}=t^{-Nr}U_{z,r}[1/t]$. Writing $S_{z,r}$ for the actual condensed stalkFrobenius, this proves
$$b_zS_{z,r}=\rho_{E,s}(F_x^{(r)})b_z.$$
This applies to every embedding and its corresponding lift, as in Step 7. The point realization sends each differential and each operator matrix through $E\to\Omega$, so its induced maps on cohomology are the stated scalar extensions.

source.place: Clause (4), local operator; point-coefficient comparison and pullback composition supply its condensed interpretation

proof.text: For any of the bounded finite-dimensional coefficient complexes just compared, [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace] gives a right dual of its finite-matrix realization, and explicitly gives one for every isomorphic object. Apply this to $b_M$ and to each $b_z$. They are isomorphisms in $D^b_c(s)[[\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)]]$, so the required right duals lie in this same category. Its cohomology comparison also identifies the realized cohomology spaces and induced operators with ordinary scalar extension. Only these realization and duality clauses are used; there is no use of its trace calculation or of a trace-formula theorem. All comparisons are natural because $J$, coefficient extension, the compact-support comparison, pullback comparison, and $\beta$ are natural; hence they provide the functorial realization and the specified operator isomorphisms asserted in the statement.
